commands.name: nav.open
commands.desc: Open the pane / window navigator

commands.name: nav.goto
commands.desc: Focus a pane (local) or window (relay) by descriptor

commands.name: nav.next
commands.desc: Focus the next pane in this skin

commands.name: nav.prev
commands.desc: Focus the previous pane in this skin

commands.name: nav.back
commands.desc: Return focus to the previously focused pane

commands.name: pane.close
commands.desc: Close the focused pane

commands.name: killring.open
commands.desc: Open the kill-ring picker (also panel-frame killring key: Esc-y)

commands.name: tree.open
commands.desc: Open the file tree pane (endpoint ③)

commands.name: tree.add
commands.desc: tree skin: add a slot for <path> (default: the directory selected in the tree)

commands.name: tree.del
commands.desc: tree skin: remove slot <n>

commands.name: tree.order
commands.desc: tree skin: swap slots <a> and <b>

commands.name: tree.tag
commands.desc: tree skin: tag slot <n> (no tag: clear it)

commands.name: tree.update
commands.desc: tree skin: read the slots file again, tidy it (order, 1..n), refresh the tree

commands.name: tree.edit
commands.desc: tree skin: open <path> in code_editor (default: the slots file)

commands.name: code.write
commands.desc: code_editor: save (bang: without checking the disk) -- :w in a skin's input form

commands.name: code.edit
commands.desc: code_editor: open <path> (a new file when it does not exist; no path: read it again) -- :e

commands.name: code.delete
commands.desc: code_editor: delete the file on disk (the text stays) -- :Delete

commands.name: code.rename
commands.desc: code_editor: rename in the same directory -- :Rename

commands.name: code.move
commands.desc: code_editor: move to <path> -- :Move

commands.name: code.to-input
commands.desc: code_editor: to the skin's input line (as vim's :#; emacs' M-x)

commands.name: code.scratch
commands.desc: code_editor: write this text over the scratch (~work/scratch); the file here is untouched -- :Scratch

commands.name: code.replace
commands.desc: code_editor: every <mark> in the text replaced with an id of the relay's list <list> (never handed out twice), one change -- :Replace <mark> <list> (with: "<mark> <list>"; :w replace <mark> <list> saves after)

commands.name: code.mirror
commands.desc: code_editor: write the copy of the text now (~/.local/state/tezcatl/mirror) -- :Mirror

commands.name: code.replay
commands.desc: code_editor: put the copy into the text (one undo step) -- :Replay

commands.name: code.reconnect
commands.desc: code_editor: the language server went away -- copy, open the file again (attached again), replay the copy -- :Reconnect

commands.name: mirror.list
commands.desc: file_changes: read the copies left by code_editor closed with unsaved edits again, and go there (Enter opens one: :Replay, :w; d d throws one away)

commands.name: mirror.drop
commands.desc: file_changes: throw away the copy of <path> left by a code_editor closed unsaved (never one a code_editor holds now)

commands.name: code.lsp-definition
commands.desc: code_editor: go to the definition of what is under the cursor (another file: code.open-at) -- :LspDef

commands.name: code.lsp-references
commands.desc: code_editor: every use of what is under the cursor, in a list (Enter opens one) -- :LspRefs

commands.name: code.lsp-rename
commands.desc: code_editor: rename the symbol under the cursor to <name> (other files it reaches are opened in code_editor and edited unsaved; all or nothing) -- :LspRename name

commands.name: code.lsp-format
commands.desc: code_editor: format the file as the language server does -- :LspFormat

commands.name: code.lsp-hover
commands.desc: code_editor: the language server's description of what is under the cursor (vim K) -- written whole in the lsp_log panel of the skin; a line in the code_editor header

commands.name: code.diag-next
commands.desc: code_editor: the next diagnostic in this file, wrapping around (vim ]d)

commands.name: code.diag-prev
commands.desc: code_editor: the previous diagnostic in this file (vim [d)

commands.name: code.def-next
commands.desc: code_editor: the next definition -- the outline's (vim ]])

commands.name: code.def-prev
commands.desc: code_editor: the previous definition (vim [[)

commands.name: code.node-select
commands.desc: code_editor: select the syntax node under the cursor; again: its parent (Lezer grammars)

commands.name: code.node-parent
commands.desc: code_editor: the cursor to the start of the parent syntax node

commands.name: code.node-next
commands.desc: code_editor: the cursor to the next sibling syntax node

commands.name: code.node-prev
commands.desc: code_editor: the cursor to the previous sibling syntax node

commands.name: lsp.back
commands.desc: the lsp_log panel of the skin: back to where the last LSP jump left from (vim C-o)

commands.name: lsp.forward
commands.desc: the lsp_log panel of the skin: forward again, where that jump went (vim C-i)

commands.name: code.grep
commands.desc: search the files under <path> (the FS root by default) for <pattern> (ripgrep, smart case); the matches in a list, Enter opens one -- :grep pattern [path]

commands.name: code.list
commands.desc: code_editor: the list of the code_editor windows open now (Enter goes to one)

commands.name: code.find
commands.desc: code_editor: is <path> open in a code_editor? (which ones)

commands.name: skin.add
commands.desc: frame: add <panel> (as skin add <panel> in its input form: the panel's own place, else the focused line)

commands.name: skin.read
commands.desc: frame: read the skin kept under <name> (as skin read <name> in its input form; the skin_list panel's M-r)

commands.name: skin.focus
commands.desc: frame: focus abs (the map -- the lead-key shortcut ;:), x or y (as skin focus <place> in its input form; a place of two words, 2 3, is typed there)

commands.name: dock.target
commands.desc: frame: to the input_target of the dock, where a letter picks where the input form sends (the lead-key shortcut ;i); the choice brings the keyboard back to the input form

commands.name: dock.suggest
commands.desc: frame: to the source of the suggestions in the dock (@gsel; the lead-key shortcut ;g), where up / down turn it and a letter picks it and brings the keyboard back; Enter goes into the suggestions

commands.name: dock.recv
commands.desc: frame: to the output_target of the dock, where a letter picks where the receiving side takes its lines from (the lead-key shortcut ;o); the choice brings the keyboard back. While the keyboard is in the input form, the receiving side follows where it sends

commands.name: work.list
commands.desc: the record of what is running and what ran, in a list (the frame adds a work panel; else a new window)

commands.name: work.cancel
commands.desc: stop row <n> of the work list (the pair's cancel, sent to who fired it)

commands.name: check.update-all
commands.desc: frame: every code_editor of the frame used last compares what it opened with the disk -- check update all (an intent's post.commands after a checkout or a pull: D-intent-later)

commands.name: juncture.set
commands.desc: juncture: put the file of the code_editor meant now in the index, its text the start (j0) -- the frame's juncture set

commands.name: juncture.point
commands.desc: juncture: keep the text of the code_editor meant now as a point, a child of the current one -- juncture point

commands.name: juncture.back
commands.desc: juncture: put the parent of the current point into the code_editor meant now, unsaved (the text now is kept first) -- juncture back

commands.name: juncture.forward
commands.desc: juncture: put the child taken last into the code_editor meant now, unsaved -- juncture forward

commands.name: juncture.tree
commands.desc: juncture: the juncture_tree panel of the file of the code_editor meant now (the one in the frame shows it, else one is added) -- juncture tree

commands.name: markdown.open
commands.desc: markdown: a markdown panel for the note <path> (its saved text; each time a new panel) -- the frame's markdown <path>

commands.name: markdown.follow
commands.desc: markdown: the markdown panel meant now follows the code_editor of this skin that has its note (its unsaved text, its cursor) -- markdown follow

commands.name: markdown.unfollow
commands.desc: markdown: the markdown panel meant now shows the saved text again -- markdown unfollow

commands.name: image.show
commands.desc: image: the image panel of the frame used last shows the picture at <path> (a file of the pages, e.g. assets/tezcatlipoca.png); none there: one is added -- the frame's image <path>

commands.name: task_table.save
commands.desc: task_table: the task_table meant now saved to its book (w) -- the frame's task_table save

commands.name: task_table.put
commands.desc: task_table: the task_table meant now saved and put into its note (W); refused when the note's table changed since it was taken -- task_table put

commands.name: task_table.list
commands.desc: task_table: the task_table meant now saved, and the rows it shows (its filter, its order) cut into the task list -- the agenda (L) -- task_table list

commands.name: run.start
commands.desc: run: the run_table meant now sends its rows, the smallest id with an empty status first (R) -- run start

commands.name: run.stop
commands.desc: run: the run_table meant now writes stop in every empty status (S) -- run stop

commands.name: minimum.open
commands.desc: a code_vi_minimum at the end of the frame: a sentence written, sent with :m (input / xterm / code_editor <file> / back) -- the frame's minimum

commands.name: go.on
commands.desc: the frame: go to what the last line of the receiving side with a reference (@...) points at -- a panel (focused), a place in a file (code.open-at) -- go on in its input form

commands.name: code.goto
commands.desc: code_editor: the cursor to <line>[:<col>] (1-based) in the code_editor focused last; with <path>, code.open-at -- :12 in a skin's input form

commands.name: code.open-at
commands.desc: code_editor: go to the code_editor that has <path> open (a new one when none has), at <line>:<col> -- :find path[:line[:col]]

commands.name: matrix.update
commands.desc: matrix: fetch the table shown again (a matrix_set's, else the latest matrix.html)

commands.name: matrix.get
commands.desc: matrix: fetch the table at <path> (kind:ref[@root]); with no table open, open a new matrix.html

commands.name: color.show
commands.desc: color: turn the colour panels the colour given ({color}, or {json, name}: the colour <name> of a JSON from the FS root); with none open, open a new color.html

commands.name: matrix.pwd
commands.desc: matrix: show the path of the table shown
